headline: Geopolitical Shock Rattles Equities as Semis and Energy Buck a Broad Retreat
body_html:
Tuesday's session closed on a sour note for most of Wall Street, with decliners outnumbering advancers by more than two to one — 376 names fell against just 168 that managed gains across a universe of 545 names. The dominant force was unmistakable: escalating Middle East tensions, after Iran-backed Houthi forces struck four Saudi cities in what analysts described as a significant widening of the regional conflict. Oil prices surged on the news, stoking fresh inflation anxiety that weighed on rate-sensitive and consumer-facing corners of the market.

The sector scorecard told a stark story. Homebuilders bore the heaviest losses, off roughly 3%, while Software shed more than 2% and Consumer names fell nearly as much. Healthcare also retreated sharply, weighed down by broad-based selling in medical-device and pharmaceutical shares. The lone bright spots were Semiconductors, which added 1.38%, and Energy, which climbed 0.63% as crude's advance lifted fuel-cell and solar plays alike.

Semtech led all advancers, surging nearly 10%, with optical-networking peer Coherent and glass specialist Corning each posting gains above 7%. On the downside, Stryker surrendered almost 9% to claim the session's worst performance. With geopolitical risk now firmly at the fore and inflation fears rekindled, the market's appetite for defensiveness deserves close attention heading into Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strike on Saudi Cities Jolts Energy Markets
briefs.body: Iran-backed Houthi forces attacked four Saudi cities Tuesday in what Reuters described as a notable expansion of the Middle East conflict, leaving 73 people injured. The assault sent oil prices sharply higher and rattled equity markets broadly, reigniting concerns about supply disruptions and their knock-on effect on global inflation.

briefs.headline: Semtech Surges Nearly 10% to Lead the Tape
briefs.body: Analog semiconductor maker Semtech was Tuesday's standout mover, jumping close to 10% to top all gainers in the session. Optical-networking equipment maker Coherent added 7.1%, suggesting continued investor appetite for connectivity infrastructure tied to data-center buildout themes that have driven the group over the past several years.

briefs.headline: Solar Names Shine as Energy Complex Catches a Bid
briefs.body: Bloom Energy soared 9.63% and ranked as the second-best performer of the session, while Enphase Energy and SolarEdge each added more than 6.5%. Options market activity in alternative energy names has been notably elevated, reflecting growing speculative interest in the sector as Middle East risk drives energy-price volatility.

briefs.headline: Stryker Leads Healthcare's Sharp Decline
briefs.body: Medical-device maker Stryker fell 8.81%, the steepest single-name drop of the day, as the Healthcare sector overall shed 1.78%. The selling appeared broad across device and pharmaceutical sub-sectors, consistent with a risk-off rotation that punished defensive-growth names carrying elevated valuations heading into the session.

briefs.headline: Software Selloff Hits Automation and Finance SaaS Hardest
briefs.body: The Software sector dropped 2.13% on Tuesday, with BlackLine and UiPath each declining roughly 7.8% to rank among the session's worst performers. Shopify, an e-commerce platform, also slid 7.57%, suggesting that growth-oriented technology names faced broad multiple compression as inflation fears resurfaced alongside the day's geopolitical headlines.

briefs.headline: US and UK Tighten Sanctions Pressure on Iran
briefs.body: The United States Treasury unveiled sweeping new aviation-related sanctions targeting Iran on Tuesday, while the United Kingdom separately published legislation aimed at imposing tougher measures over Tehran's nuclear programme. The dual-front regulatory push added another layer of uncertainty to an already tense geopolitical backdrop that markets are now pricing with increasing urgency.
